title: Undoing a square
objectives: Find square and cube roots by undoing a power
Estimate a root between two whole numbers

screens.prose: A square floor is covered by 36 equal tiles. You cannot see the joins between them.
screens.question: How many tiles run along one side?

hints.text: Which number times itself makes 36?
Try 5 and 7: $5 \times 5 = 25$ and $7 \times 7 = 49$.

feedback.correct: Six rows of six tiles make 36.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number that, multiplied by itself, gives 36.

byKey.halved: You halved 36. Halving undoes doubling, not squaring: $18 \times 18 = 324$.
byKey.quartered: You divided by 4, as if the tiles ran round the edge. They cover the whole floor: $9 \times 9 = 81$.
byKey.third: You divided by 3. Check by squaring: $12 \times 12 = 144$, not 36.

explain.text: You looked for a side that, squared, gives 36. Since $6 \times 6 = 36$, the side is 6 tiles. You undid a square.

screens.prose: The curve pairs every side length with the area of its square. Drag the point along the curve and watch the area change.
screens.question: Find the side of a square with area 49.

hints.text: Watch the area as you drag. Stop when it reads 49.
The area passes 49 between sides 6 and 8.

feedback.correct: A side of 7 gives an area of 49.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drag until the label reads area 49.

byKey.low: A side of 6.5 gives an area of 42.25. Keep going right.
byKey.high: A side of 7.5 gives an area of 56.25. That is past 49.
byKey.half: That side gives an area under 26. Drag further right, until the area reads 49.

explain.text: You searched along the curve for an area of 49 and read off the side, 7. That reverses squaring, since $7^2 = 49$.

screens.prose: Undoing a square is taking a **square root**. We write $\surd{49} = 7$, because $7^2 = 49$. The dashed line marks an area of 64.
screens.question: What is $\sqrt{64}$?

options.why: You halved 64. Check by squaring: $32^2 = 1{,}024$, not 64.
That is the cube root, since $4^3 = 64$. The square root needs $8 \times 8$.
You squared 64. The root goes the other way: which number squared gives 64?

hints.text: Which number times itself is 64?
The dashed line at area 64 meets the curve above one side length.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the side whose square is 64.

byKey.halved: You halved 64. Square rooting is not halving: check $32^2$.

explain.text: $8 \times 8 = 64$, so $\surd{64} = 8$. A square root asks which side gives this area. Check any root by squaring it back.

screens.prose: 50 is not a square number, so $\surd{50}$ is not a whole number. The dots mark $7^2 = 49$ and $8^2 = 64$.
screens.question: Where is $\sqrt{50}$?

options.why: You split the gap evenly. But 50 is 1 above 49 and 14 below 64, so the root sits near 7.
$7^2 = 49$ is below 50, so the side for 50 must be a little longer than 7.
You halved 50. Square rooting is not halving: $25^2 = 625$.

hints.text: Which square numbers sit either side of 50?
$7^2 = 49$ and $8^2 = 64$. The dashed line crosses the curve between them.
50 is 1 above 49 and 14 below 64, so the root is just above 7.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare 50 with the squares either side of it.

byKey.halfway: You split the gap evenly. 50 is far closer to 49 than to 64, so the root is close to 7.

explain.text: $49 < 50 < 64$, so $7 < \surd{50} < 8$. Since 50 is much closer to 49, the root is just above 7: $\surd{50} \approx 7.07$. Check: $7.07^2 \approx 49.98$.

screens.prose: A cube root undoes a cube: ${}^3\!\surd{27} = 3$ because $3^3 = 27$. The table lists squares and cubes.
screens.question: What is $\sqrt[3]{125}$?

hints.text: Find 125 in the $n^3$ column.
125 sits in the row for $n = 5$.
$5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number that, used three times, multiplies to 125.

byKey.square-root: You took the square root. A cube root needs a number used three times: $5 \times 5 \times 5$.
byKey.thirded: You divided by 3. Check by cubing: $41.67^3$ is about 72,000.

explain.text: You read the table backwards: find 125 among the cubes, then read $n$. Since $5^3 = 125$, ${}^3\!\surd{125} = 5$.

screens.prose: 100 is not in the cube column. Its cube root lies between two whole numbers.
screens.question: Between which whole numbers is $\sqrt[3]{100}$?

options.why: You took the square root: $\sqrt{100} = 10$. A cube root needs $n^3$ near 100.
$5^3 = 125$ is already above 100, so the root is below 5.

hints.text: Which cubes in the table sit either side of 100?

feedback.correct: $64 < 100 < 125$, so the root is between 4 and 5.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the cubes either side of 100.

explain.text: $64 < 100 < 125$, so $4 < {}^3\!\surd{100} < 5$. In fact ${}^3\!\surd{100} \approx 4.64$. Cubes grow fast, so cube roots stay small.

screens.prose: A square of area 0.25 sits in the corner of a 1 by 1 square. Each small square is 0.1 by 0.1. Most people expect the side to be smaller than 0.25.

state.caption: Find the side of a square of area 0.25

screens.question: How long is its side?

hints.text: Each small square has area $0.1 \times 0.1 = 0.01$. How many make 0.25?
25 small squares fill a 5 by 5 corner.
A side of 5 small squares is 0.5. Check: $0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25$.

feedback.correct: $0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25$: the side is longer than the area is big.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count how many small squares make 0.25, then read the side.

byKey.halved: You halved 0.25. Square 0.125 to check: you get about 0.016, not 0.25.
byKey.squared: You squared 0.25. The root goes the other way: which number times itself is 0.25?
byKey.tiny: $0.05 \times 0.05 = 0.0025$, far too small. Count the small squares: 25 of the 100 make 0.25.

explain.text: 25 small squares fill a 5 by 5 corner, so the side is 0.5. Check: $0.5^2 = 0.25$. Between 0 and 1, a square root is bigger than the number.

screens.prose: Every time, you undid a power. $$\surd{a} = b \text{ means } b^2 = a \text{ and } b \ge 0 \qquad {}^3\!\surd{a} = c \text{ means } c^3 = a$$ When $a$ is not a perfect square, find the square numbers either side of it.
screens.question: Between which whole numbers is $\sqrt{30}$?

options.why: You halved 30. Check: $15^2 = 225$, far more than 30.
$5^2 = 25$ is below 30, so the root is above 5.
You stayed near 30. The root is a side length, and $29^2$ is 841.

hints.text: Which square numbers sit either side of 30?
$25 < 30 < 36$, so the root is between 5 and 6.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the squares either side of 30.

explain.text: $5^2 = 25$ and $6^2 = 36$ sit either side of 30. So $5 < \surd{30} < 6$; in fact $\surd{30} \approx 5.48$.

screens.prose: Pin down $\surd{20}$ to one decimal place without a calculator.
screens.question: Put the lines of the argument in order.

lines.text: $16 < 20 < 25$, the square numbers either side of 20
$\sqrt{16} < \sqrt{20} < \sqrt{25}$, a bigger square has a longer side

hints.text: Start with numbers you know: the squares near 20.
Square roots keep the order: a bigger area has a longer side.
Squares, then roots, then whole numbers, then narrow it with decimals.

feedback.correct: $\sqrt{20}$ is between 4.4 and 4.5; it is about 4.47.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each line should follow from the one above it.

byKey.narrow: Narrowing to tenths comes last, once you know the root is between 4 and 5.

explain.text: You trapped 20 between squares, took roots, then squared two tries to narrow it. $\surd{20} \approx 4.47$, since $4.47^2 \approx 19.98$. Squaring a guess is always the check.

screens.prose: A fund's daily returns swing by about 1%. Risk grows with the square root of time, so over 252 trading days the swing is about $0.01 \times \surd{252}$.
screens.question: Roughly how big is the yearly swing?

hints.text: Which square numbers sit either side of 252?
252 is close to 256, so $\sqrt{252}$ is just under 16. Multiply by 1%.

feedback.correct: $\sqrt{252} \approx 15.9$, so a 1% daily swing is about 16% a year.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Estimate $\sqrt{252}$ first, then multiply by 1%.

byKey.no-root: You multiplied by 252, as if risk grew in a straight line. It grows with $\sqrt{252}$, about 16.
byKey.halved: You halved 252. Square rooting is not halving: $126^2$ is nearly 16,000.
byKey.hundred: You found the root but divided by 100 once too often. $15.9 \times 1\%$ is 15.9%.

explain.text: $225 < 252 < 256$, so $\surd{252}$ is just under 16; it is about 15.87. A 1% daily swing becomes roughly 16% over a year, not 252%. Risk grows like the square root of time.

ideas: A square root undoes a square: $\surd{a}$ is the side of a square with area $a$.
To estimate a root, find the square numbers either side, then see which one is closer.
A cube root undoes a cube. For numbers between 0 and 1, roots are bigger than the number.

formula.name: Square root
formula.note: Check a root by squaring it back.

summary.trap: Square rooting is not halving: $\sqrt{64} = 8$, not 32. And $\sqrt{0.25} = 0.5$ is bigger than 0.25.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which number times itself is 81?

byKey.halved: You halved 81. Check by squaring: $40.5^2$ is over 1,600.
byKey.squared: You squared 81. The root goes the other way.

options.why: $9^2 = 81$ is below 90, so the root is above 9.
You divided by 3. $30^2 = 900$, ten times too big.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the squares either side of 90.

explain.text: $9^2 = 81$ and $10^2 = 100$ sit either side of 90. So $9 < \surd{90} < 10$; it is about 9.49.

quiz.prose: Think of a square inside a 1 by 1 square.
quiz.question: What is $\sqrt{0.09}$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which decimal times itself gives 0.09?

byKey.halved: You halved 0.09. Square rooting is not halving.
byKey.kept-zeros: You took the root of 9 and kept the 0.0 in front. $0.03^2 = 0.0009$.
byKey.squared: You squared 0.09. The root goes the other way.

explain.text: $0.3 \times 0.3 = 0.09$, so $\surd{0.09} = 0.3$. As with 0.25, the root of a number below 1 is bigger than the number.

quiz.question: Which values of $x$ make this true?

options.why: $(-7)^2 = 49$ too: a negative times a negative is positive. The symbol $\sqrt{49}$ names only the positive one.
You halved 49. Squaring is not doubling.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Square each candidate and check.

explain.text: $7 \times 7 = 49$ and $(-7) \times (-7) = 49$. So $x = 7$ or $x = -7$. The root sign $\surd{49}$ means the positive one, 7: that is the edge case.

quiz.prose: A cube is built from 8,000 small cubes.
quiz.question: How many small cubes run along one edge?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which number, used three times, multiplies to 8,000?

byKey.square-root: You took the square root. A cube needs three equal factors.
byKey.thirded: You divided by 3. Cubing that gives billions.
